vopros: What do you know about WorldSpeak School in Los Angeles? Is it a good choice for my child?

vyzhimka.tekst:
WorldSpeak is an interesting option, particularly if multilingual immersion is a high priority, but there’s an important distinction between its preschool and its elementary program that I would investigate before enrolling.

WorldSpeak has operated on the Westside for roughly 25 years. Its main Westwood location is at 1639 Westwood Blvd., and it has a newer Pico location at 10747 W. Pico Blvd. The school emphasizes language immersion—currently advertising Spanish, Mandarin Chinese, French, Russian, and English—alongside play, music, art, and academics. It also offers math and chess enrichment. ([worldspeakschool.com](https://worldspeakschool.com/?utm_source=openai))

For preschool, there are several encouraging signs. The Westwood preschool is a California-licensed child-care center. In its November 6, 2024 unannounced state inspection, it had 22 children enrolled with a licensed capacity of 22; the report notes appropriate sanitation, safe storage of hazardous materials, functioning child facilities, and other required safety measures. The newer Pico preschool is also currently licensed by California and has a capacity of 60. ([ccld.dss.ca.gov](https://www.ccld.dss.ca.gov/transparencyapi/api/FacilityReports?facNum=197418648&inx=1&utm_source=openai))

Parent feedback is generally quite positive, though the samples aren't huge. Recent aggregated Yelp results show roughly 4.5 stars, with parents repeatedly praising caring teachers, the community, and language instruction. There are also some negative reviews criticizing organization, communication/management, and whether the advertised curriculum matches the day-to-day experience. I would take both sides seriously rather than relying heavily on the star rating. ([local.yahoo.com](https://local.yahoo.com/info-169320304-worldspeak-los-angeles?utm_source=openai))

One thing I would specifically clarify if you're considering kindergarten or elementary school: the California Department of Education lists "WorldSpeak Language Immersion Private School," formerly K–5, as closed effective June 30, 2025. Yet WorldSpeak's current website continues to advertise elementary and transitional-kindergarten programs, and some private-school directories currently describe a very small K–3 program. Those facts aren't necessarily contradictory—it could have reorganized, changed its filing/entity, or shifted how the program operates—but I would want WorldSpeak to explain the current elementary school's legal/registration status before enrolling. ([cde.ca.gov](https://www.cde.ca.gov/SchoolDirectory/details?cdscode=19647336154249&utm_source=openai))

My preliminary assessment would therefore be:

- For a 2–5-year-old: WorldSpeak is definitely worth touring if you want genuine exposure to a second language. Its longevity, licensed preschool operation, small Westwood setting, and generally strong parent feedback are meaningful positives. ([ccld.dss.ca.gov](https://www.ccld.dss.ca.gov/transparencyapi/api/FacilityReports?facNum=197418648&inx=1&utm_source=openai))
- For elementary age: I'd investigate considerably more before making it your child's primary school, particularly because of the June 2025 closure record and the extremely small enrollment reported by third-party sources. ([cde.ca.gov](https://www.cde.ca.gov/SchoolDirectory/details?cdscode=19647336154249&utm_source=openai))
- For a child who thrives in intimate, individualized environments: the small-school atmosphere could be a significant advantage.
- For a family primarily seeking a traditional, larger independent-school environment—with extensive facilities, larger peer cohorts, sports, specialists, etc.—WorldSpeak may be less compelling.

One other thing I'd pay attention to on a tour is what "immersion" actually means in your child's particular classroom. Ask how many hours per day the target language is used, whether the lead teacher is fluent/native-level, how much staff turnover they've had in the past two years, class size and teacher-child ratio, and where graduates typically go afterward. Their website describes substantial immersion, but those concrete questions tell you far more about what your child will actually experience. ([worldspeakschool.com](https://worldspeakschool.com/?utm_source=openai))

If you tell me your child's age, which language you're interested in (Spanish, Mandarin, Russian, French, etc.), roughly where in LA you live, and what matters most to you—academics, warmth/nurturing, language fluency, preparation for competitive private schools, cost—I can give you a much more useful assessment of WorldSpeak and compare it with the strongest alternatives nearby.
